title: Reviewing AI-assisted code with production ownership in mind
summary: A practical review approach for generated changes: define the behavior, inspect the assumptions, and verify the paths that matter.
bodyHtml:
AI coding tools can shorten the path from an idea to an implementation. Accepting the result still requires a clear understanding of the system and the change being made.

Define the behavior before the implementation

Write down the outcome, the relevant constraints, and the behavior that existing users depend on. Those details give both the tool and the reviewer something concrete to work against.

Read the assumptions

I review generated code for the same concerns I would raise in any pull request: data ownership, error handling, dependencies, naming, and fit with the surrounding code. A plausible implementation can still rely on an assumption that the application does not support.

If I cannot explain a section of the change, I need to investigate it before accepting it. Confidence in the tool does not answer questions about what the application will do.

Verify a manageable change

Focused changes are easier to inspect and exercise. Verification should cover the intended behavior and the failures that could affect users, using tests or direct checks appropriate to the risk.

Consider the next operational problem

Before shipping, I want to know how a failure will become visible and how the change could be reversed. Those questions remain part of engineering ownership regardless of how the code was produced.
